FIELD NOTE / 03

Will a big ticketing platform sell your show? For most new organisers, no

A big marketplace listing feels like free reach. For a new organiser, it rarely is: your tickets are sold by your posts, your groups and your people. The 2-minute version, with a checklist.

LOHITESH · 16 OCTOBER 2026
IN THIS STORY
1. Nobody browses for a debut show2. Your buyers come from you3. What that listing really costs youProof: a sold-out room, no marketplaceYour 4-step checklist
BACK TO THE JOURNAL ↗

  • People open ticketing apps to buy what they already chose, not to discover new shows.

  • For a new organiser, your own posts and groups sell the tickets. The platform is just the checkout.

  • So the commission buys you very little. Keep your margin and your audience.

1. Nobody browses for a debut show

People open a ticketing app to book a film, a big concert or a match. Search, pay, leave.

The top of the screen goes to headline acts. India had 70 to 80 concert days with 10,000+ crowds in a year (FICCI-EY), and those days take the banners. A debut show sits far below, often behind paid placements.

2. Your buyers come from you

Where buyers find your showWho did the work
Instagram posts and ReelsYou
WhatsApp and community groupsYou
Email to past attendeesYou
Friends telling friendsYour audience
Browsing the marketplace appRarely, for a new name

The numbers agree. Event creators who tracked their sales traced 45% of tickets to email alone, and about a quarter of page visits to social media. And 52% of event-goers say they find events on social media.

3. What that listing really costs you

  • The cut: commission per ticket, often with an extra fee for the buyer on top.

  • Lost buyers: forced sign-ups, surprise fees at the last step, other shows recommended on your page.

  • Lost audience: on many marketplaces the buyer's details stay with the platform, so you can't reach them next time.

You make the poster, the Reel and the messages. Why pay someone else for the reach you built?

Proof: a sold-out room, no marketplace

Veda Nāda's Mantra Mādhurya sold out a ninety-seat room in Bengaluru with one ticket link shared with their own community. No banner, no paid placement.

Your 4-step checklist

  1. Own your ticket page: your name on it, one tap on a phone, UPI, no forced account.

  2. Keep every buyer's contact, so show two starts with the crowd from show one.

  3. Spend the saved commission on a boosted post, a better poster or a fairer artist fee.

  4. Add a marketplace later, once people search for your name. Until then you pay for reach you don't get.

Sources: FICCI-EY Media & Entertainment Report 2025; a 2018 survey of event creators by a global self-serve ticketing company; a 2021 YouGov survey of US event-goers.
